candidates.section: Current flag of Greece > Flag days
candidates.text: Ohi Day decorations in Poros Law 851/1978 sets the general outline for when the specific days on which the flag should be raised. For national holidays, this applies country-wide, but on local ones it only applies to those areas where the said holiday is being celebrated. Additionally, the flag may also be flown on days of national mourning, half-mast. The Minister of the Interior has the authority to proclaim flag days if they are not already proclaimed, and proclaiming regional flag days is vested with the elected head of each regional unit (formerly prefectures). {| class="wikitable" style=

It was not popular during its period of official use, as Cretans wanted union with Greece, and was de facto abolished following the island's unilateral proclamation of union with Greece in September 1908.
! scope="row" | | 1897–1898 | Cretan revolutionary flag of the 1897 revolt. |
! scope="row" | | 1878–1885 | Flag of Eastern Rumelia in Northern Thrace. | Three horizontal stripes red, white, and blue.

! scope="row" | | 1878 | Flag of the 1878 Cretan Insurrection. | The design of the flag above is a series of six stripes, the blue ones only stretching to 4/5 of the flag. The banner contains the words "ΗΤΑΝ ΗΕΠΙΤΑΝ" (expression of the Spartan women, when they would send off their sons into war implying: [I will wait for you] either with this [the shield, victorious], or on this [wounded or dead]) on the second white stripe, followed by a likely date of the rebellion, August 16, on the third white stripe. On the first two stripes, on the extreme corner, a Greek cross is displayed.
! scope="row" | | 1878 | Flag of West Macedonia during the 1878 revolt. |

! scope="row" | Flag used during the siege of Arkadi | 1866 | Flag used in the Arkadi Monastery by Christian Cretans supporting union with Greece, during the Great Cretan Revolt of 1866–1869. | The flag consists of the plain cross version of the Greek national flag, featuring the initials of the motto Κρήτη, Ένωσις, Ελευθερία ή Θάνατος ("Crete, Enosis, Freedom or Death"), and the cross with the inscription ΙΣ ΧΣ ΝΙΚΑ ("Jesus Christ Conquers").

candidates.file: Flag of the United States of the Ionian Islands.svg
candidates.text: ! scope="row" | Flag of the Ionian Islands under British rule | 1817–1864 | Flag of the United States of the Ionian Islands, a British protectorate from 1815 until its unity with Greece in 1864. | The flag is a variation of the British colonial Blue Ensign, with red bordering. It is defaced with the islands' emblem, a variant of the Venetian "Lion of St. Mark" holding seven bundled arrows, representing the unity of the seven Ionian Islands, with the Bible superimposed on them.

! scope="row" | Flag of the Septinsular Republic | 1800–1807 | Flag of the Septinsular Republic, the first modern Greek self-governing state, comprising the Ionian Islands, under joint Russian and Ottoman suzerainty. | The flag depicts the "Lion of St. Mark", the symbol of the Republic of Venice, under whose rule the Ionian Islands were until 1797. The lion holds seven bundled arrows, representing the unity of the seven islands, with the Bible superimposed on them.

! scope="row" | | rowspan="2" | 1807 | Flag of captain Ioannis Stathas, designed in the island of Skiathos. It resembles the old flag and the jack of the Hellenic Navy. | White cross on an azure field.

! scope="row" | | Flag of Central Macedonia designed by chieftain Nikolaos Tsamis against the Ottoman Empire. | An azure Greek cross on a white field. The flag also bore the inscription: "Σημαία Ελληνική, Νικόλαος Τσάμης" (Greek Flag, Nikolaos Tsamis).

! scope="row" | | c.a 1800 | Flag of the Kallergis family used before the revolution. | The flag shares a lot of similarities with the current flag and bears the phrase "EN TOYTΩ NIKA" (In hoc signo vinces, eng: In this sign thou shalt conquer). Heraldic ensembles containing the Kallergis family coat of arms (bendy argent and azure) can be found all over the island of Crete, in churches and other monuments.

! scope="row" | Flag of the Maniots | c.a 1793 | Flag proposed by Rigas Feraios for his envisioned pan-Balkan Federation. | Three red, white, and black horizontal stripes. Red stands for the imperial purple, white for the righteousness of the fight against tyranny, and black for the death in the struggle for liberty. It also features three crosses for the Christian nations of the Balkans, and the club of Hercules in the middle.

! scope="row" | | 1774–1800s | This flag, the so-called "Graeco-Ottoman" ensign (Γραικοθωμανική παντιέρα), was allowed for use by Greek merchant ships during the latter stages of Ottoman rule. | The flag consists of three horizontal stripes in the colours red (for the Ottoman Empire), blue (for the Greeks), and red.

! scope="row" | | 1770–1821 | This design appeared in the Orlov revolt, based on older patterns.
